name: Stupice Tomato

companions.note: Repels tomato hornworm; attracts pollinators and predatory insects. Classic pairing.
May improve flavor; repels aphids and whitefly

antagonists.note: Brassicas and tomatoes compete as heavy feeders and may suppress each other
Alliums can stunt tomato growth when planted too close

pnw_notes: Czech heirloom bred for cool, short-season climates — one of the most reliable heirlooms for PNW summers. Small to medium red fruits with excellent flavor. Indeterminate: will keep growing and fruiting until frost, needs sturdy cage or stake. Start indoors in late February for maximum season length. Consistent watering critical — irregular moisture causes blossom end rot and cracking.

planting_windows.notes: Start 6–8 weeks before last frost; use greenhouse to harden off before transplanting
After last frost (May 1–15 for Portland); soil should be consistently warm
Harvest when fully colored and slightly soft to the touch; continue until first frost
